articles.title: In New York, 29 million discarded glass bottles were ground into concrete for JPMorgan Chase’s 60-storey headquarters; replacing 40% of its cement cut over 5,000 tons of carbon and enhanced concrete strength
articles.summary: A massive skyscraper rising in Midtown Manhattan has turned tens of millions of used waste bottles into part of its structural support.
articles.body: A massive skyscraper rising in Midtown Manhattan has turned tens of millions of used waste bottles into part of its structural support. The project shows how city waste can replace carbon-heavy building materials on a large commercial scale. Workers used special concrete containing ground recycled glass in the foundation and floor slabs of JPMorgan Chase's new 60-storey headquarters at 270 Park Avenue. By replacing 40 per cent of traditional Portland cement with ground-glass pozzolan, the project kept 29 million discarded bottles out of landfills while also strengthening the concrete. The change saved more than 5,000 tons of carbon dioxide emissions during construction. Traditional cement production uses energy-intensive kilns that release large amounts of greenhouse gases, making concrete one of the main sources of industrial emissions worldwide. According to technical coverage in Concrete Products magazine, the project used the processed glass mixture across the 2.2 million-square-foot tower to meet environmental goals while also meeting strict structural performance requirements.Converting municipal glass into raw materialThe ground-glass product, made under the trade name Pozzotive by Connecticut-based company Urban Mining Industries, tackles two environmental problems at the same time. Construction companies are looking for low-carbon building materials, while recycling programs across North America often struggle to process mixed-colour glass bottles. Because of contamination and sorting costs, much of this glass can end up in regional landfills. Urban Mining collects used bottles from local waste streams and processes them through a dry milling system without chemicals or water. The facility grinds the glass into a fine powder that is free of hazardous crystalline silica. When the powder is mixed into ready-mix concrete, the reactive silica in the ground glass reacts with calcium hydroxide, a weak byproduct of cement hydration. This chemical reaction turns that byproduct into dense calcium-silicate-hydrate, the main compound that gives concrete its compressive strength. Engineering analysis published in Structure Magazine found that adding the glass powder increased the concrete's final strength and long-term durability while reducing the amount of moisture that could pass through the slabs.Engineering around tight construction schedulesUsing recycled materials in high-rise concrete can create problems with setting times. Reducing the amount of Portland cement can slow early curing, which could delay floor-by-floor construction on busy urban sites. Consulting engineering firm Severud Associates designed the structural specifications for the 270 Park Avenue tower. Engineers adjusted the mix so the high amount of pozzolan concrete could reach the required early strength. This allowed contractors to maintain a fast floor-pouring schedule. "When asked by JPMorganChase to envision 270 Park Avenue as a model for the 21st century workplace, we knew Severud Structural Engineers had to give our contribution," said Fortunato Orlando, Principal at Severud Associates, in a statement about the project's engineering specifications. "The building's design included 52,000 cubic yards of concrete that substituted locally-sourced Pozzotive ground-glass pozzolan for 40% of the cement in all structural concrete except the 16,000-psi mix." Orlando added that ground-glass pozzolan has now been added directly to the engineering firm's standard master specifications for future structural projects.Establishing scale for circular constructionThe use of recycled-glass pozzolan at 270 Park Avenue is one of the largest single applications of the material in commercial real estate. Construction managers from AECOM oversaw the work at the site, working with ready-mix concrete supplier Smyrna Ready Mix to deliver thousands of truckloads of the custom glass-based mixture into central Manhattan. "Pozzotive was the centerpiece of a much larger strategy to deliver the greenest skyscraper in America, if not the world," said Max Driscoll, Vice President of Sustainability at AECOM Construction Management, while discussing the project's material supply chain. "We are extremely proud to have facilitated a market transformation for ground glass pozzolan as a leading decarbonization strategy for construction." Beyond the carbon savings during construction, the lighter colour of the glass-based concrete reflects more light than standard grey concrete. Developers expect this quality to reduce heat absorption on exposed surfaces, lowering cooling needs inside the building and helping reduce the urban heat island effect around the base of the tower. The successful project in Midtown Manhattan has also encouraged wider use of the material in the region. After the structural work at 270 Park Avenue was completed, transportation authorities in Connecticut and New York began specifying ground-glass pozzolans for public rail infrastructure and highway projects. This helped establish a permanent industrial market for municipal waste glass across the North American Northeast.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Built in 1951, Gavin Newsom’s San Francisco childhood home listed for $4.5 million after renovation; property was owned by his maternal grandfather and sold by family in the 1970s
articles.summary: California Governor Gavin Newsom’s San Francisco childhood home has hit the market for $4.5 million, decades after his family sold the property.
articles.body: California Governor Gavin Newsom’s San Francisco childhood home has hit the market for $4.5 million, decades after his family sold the property. Newsom lived in the two-level house for the first five years of his life, and the home now looks dramatically different following an extensive renovation.The 1,445-square-foot Cole Valley property, built in 1951 and situated on nearly a quarter of an acre, features panoramic views of the Golden Gate Bridge and Downtown San Francisco. The property also includes a buildable second lot, a finished cabin currently used as an artist’s studio, a rear patio and a Japanese soaking tub.Gavin Newsom's former childhood home underwent major renovationThe house was reportedly renovated nearly down to the studs after current owner Sandra McBride, founder of a public-relations firm, purchased it in 2019 for $2.8 million, according to Zillow records. McBride subsequently transformed the property while retaining its wooded, secluded setting.“As a country girl asked to live in the city, I found the best of both worlds,” McBride said in a statement, according to Mansion Global. She described the home as a “woodland refuge” surrounded by nature and located across from hiking trails in Mount Sutro Forest, while also being close to San Francisco’s cultural, sporting and nightlife attractions.Newsom has not immediately responded to requests for comment about the sale.Property was once owned by Gavin Newsom's maternal familyPublished reports say the property was originally owned by Newsom’s maternal grandfather before being inherited by his mother, Tessa. In 1967, the year Newsom was born, his father, William Newsom, listed the house as his official address while campaigning for the San Francisco Board of Supervisors.The Newsom family sold the property in the 1970s. In 1979, the new owners added redwood siding, significantly changing the exterior appearance of the San Francisco home. They reportedly held onto the property for nearly five decades before McBride purchased it in 2019.San Francisco home offers Golden Gate Bridge viewsLocated in Cole Valley, one of San Francisco’s smaller neighborhoods, the property sits near the top of the street and benefits from elevated views. Listing agent John DiDomenico of Compass San Francisco described the parcel as unusually large for the neighborhood and surrounding areas.“This is one of the biggest parcels of land that you can find in this neighborhood or in any of the adjacent neighborhoods,” DiDomenico said. He highlighted the privacy, trees, birdsong and natural surroundings, comparing the atmosphere to what buyers might expect farther north in Marin County.The main floor of the renovated two-bedroom, two-bathroom home features an open-plan kitchen, dining area and living room, with the interior flowing directly into outdoor spaces.Primary suite spans the entire second floorThe primary suite occupies the entire second level and includes a walk-in closet, meditation space and walkout deck. Large windows provide expansive views of the Golden Gate Bridge and Downtown San Francisco, adding to the appeal of the property.The landscaped grounds include a rear patio and Japanese soaking tub. DiDomenico said the wooded surroundings make the outdoor space feel particularly secluded despite the property's location within San Francisco.The second lot is also buildable and contains a small finished cabin that McBride has been using as an artist’s studio, providing additional potential for the property’s next owner.Gavin Newsom's political profile adds interest to propertyThe listing comes as Newsom remains a prominent figure in national Democratic politics and is widely discussed as a potential 2028 presidential candidate. He has also attracted national attention through public exchanges and social-media battles with President Donald Trump.For prospective buyers, however, the property's combination of Gavin Newsom’s childhood connection, Golden Gate Bridge views, privacy, substantial land and development potential is likely to be central to its appeal. The $4.5 million listing represents a significant increase from the $2.8 million McBride paid for the property in 2019.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: Australia offers $1 million reward for missing 4-year-old boy Gus Lamont nearly a year after disappearance
articles.summary: A 1 million Australian dollar reward has been announced for information that helps solve the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont, nearly a year
articles.body: A 1 million Australian dollar reward has been announced for information that helps solve the disappearance of four-year-old Gus Lamont, nearly a year after he vanished from his family’s remote property in South Australia.Gus was last seen around 5pm on September 27, 2025, playing outside his family’s home at Oak Park Station, a vast sheep property near Yunta, about 300km north-east of Adelaide. Around 30 minutes later, his grandmother went outside to call him in and found that he was missing.The disappearance triggered one of South Australia’s biggest missing-child searches. Police conducted 11 ground searches over 30 days, while aerial operations covered more than 700 square kilometres. Investigators also searched dams, mine shafts and other locations around the property, but found no trace of the boy.Police investigate possibility someone known to Gus was involvedAuthorities initially considered whether Gus may have wandered away from the property. However, after extensive searches, police said they found no evidence to support that theory. Investigators also examined the possibility of an abduction by a stranger and looked into people who had travelled through the area, neighbours and others who may have had access to the property.In February, police declared Gus's disappearance a major crime and said they believed a person living at Oak Park Station was a suspect. His parents were ruled out as suspects.Police have continued to investigate whether someone known to Gus was involved in his disappearance. The identity of the suspect has not been publicly disclosed.Police review 'anomalies' in aerial imagesInvestigators have now carried out a detailed manual review of aerial images collected during the earlier searches. Detective Superintendent Darren Fielke said police had identified "anomalies" in the imagery, according to The Guardian.Investigators are examining the images to determine whether another physical search of the property is required. Fielke has not disclosed what the anomalies show, saying releasing details could compromise the investigation.Gus Lamont disappearance: TimelineSeptember 27, 2025: Gus is last seen playing outside his family's home at Oak Park Station.September 27, 2025: Police launch a major search after he is reported missing.October 2025: The search shifts from a rescue operation to a recovery effort after no trace of Gus is found.January 2026: Police search the property and seize a vehicle, motorbike and electronic devices.February 2026: The disappearance is declared a major crime and police identify a person living at the station as a suspect.September 2026: Investigators identify "anomalies" during a manual review of aerial imagery.September 23, 2026: South Australia announces a reward of up to $1 million as Gus's parents make a public appeal.Gus's parents make emotional appealThe new developments came as Gus's parents made their first public video appeal, asking anyone with information about their son's disappearance to come forward.Police said the reward of up to $1 million is for information that leads to the conviction of the person or people responsible for Gus's disappearance, or helps locate his remains.Fielke said the reward was intended to encourage anyone with crucial information to speak to police, while acknowledging that such a large reward could also generate false leads."One million dollars is a life-changing amount of money for someone. Now is the time to come forward," Fielke said.Police have urged people with information to provide facts that could help investigators rather than speculation or theories.You use AI every day. articles.title: Stanford AI row: Students outraged as university uses AI to alter Hispanic student with Black in promotional ad
articles.summary: Stanford University used AI to change the appearance, race and gender of students in a photo before using it as a promotion for the university's
articles.body: Stanford University used AI to change the appearance, race and gender of students in a photo before using it as a promotion for the university's residential and dining offerings. The original photo had an Asian woman, a white man and a Hispanic student. But the published version had a Black woman replacing the Hispanic man and the appearance of the other two students was also altered.After this created a massive row, the university acknowledged the incident and condemned it. "We have reviewed the matter and confirmed that AI was used to alter the image in violation of university policy. Stanford's AI policy is clear: The use of AI in producing or altering images of Stanford people, events, research, facilities, or achievements is strictly prohibited," a spokesperson for Stanford University said in a email to Fox News Digital."Both the alteration and lack of disclosure in this case violate that policy. We are working with Residential and Dining Enterprises to provide additional training and ensure proper review of all materials," the spokesperson added.Omitted student says he found it funny initiallyBilly Ramirez, the student, who was removed from the photo told the Stanford Review that he was "baffled" when he saw that he was cut out of the photo. "At first, I found it hilarious that they had used AI to completely change our appearances, including my race and gender," Ramirez told the Stanford Review."But after looking at the comparison, I was also upset because I don’t agree with Stanford making those choices about how we were represented," Ramirez continued. "Seeing my identity changed and being left out of the picture made me feel, in a way, silenced and erased from a representation that was supposed to include me.""While Stanford R&DE likely believed they were subtle enough for no one to notice, fortunately, our vigilant Stanford student body cannot be fooled. The Review will continue to monitor future advertising and actions from Stanford R&DE as they learn how to use generative AI," Stanford Review said."It's kind of unacceptable. Stanford is a place that actually prides itself on having students from over 60 different countries in their incoming class. articles.title: Ukrainian man kills one, wounds four in Poland abbey knife attack
articles.summary: Ukraine’s President Zelenskyy denounces ‘horrific crime’ after 31-year-old attacks clergy, worshippers in border town.
articles.body:
One person was killed and four others injured when a man armed with a knife attacked clergy and worshippers at a Catholic monastery in southern Poland.

Police said the 31-year-old attacker, a Ukrainian national, went on a stabbing spree at the 17th-century Benedictine abbey in Jaroslaw, some 30km (19 miles) from the border with Ukraine, on Thursday morning.

The suspect, who had entered Poland from Germany earlier in the day, reportedly grabbed a knife from the abbey’s kitchen and attacked four men and one woman, including a priest in a confessional, police said.

“Three of the victims are clergy members and two are laypeople; one person has died,” said prosecutor Bozena Harasz-Wołoszyn. Two others were in “critical, life-threatening condition”.

Polish media identified the man who died as a priest. Police did not immediately confirm the identity of the deceased.

Prosecutors said the attacker was headed for a nearby border crossing back into Ukraine but instead went to the abbey.

The motive remains unclear, and doctors will assess whether he was under the influence of alcohol, Harasz-Wołoszyn said.

Polish Prime Minister Donald Tusk said the “murderer” would be “punished with the full severity of Polish law”.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy called the attack a “horrific crime”.

“The perpetrator of this evil must bear full responsibility in accordance with the law … We are shaken by this evil. Justice must be done.”

The mayor of Jaroslaw, Marcin Nazarewicz, declared a period of mourning until the end of the week.

Stabbings, particularly at religious sites, are extremely rare in Poland, one of Europe’s most Catholic countries.

articles.title: Mark Carney says he has considered possibility of US military action
articles.summary: The prime minister described the risk of an action by the country's southern neighbour as remote, but said "it would be irresponsible" not to prepare.
articles.body:
Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney has considered the remote possibility of US military action against Canada, according to an interview with The New York Times.

Carney told the Times that his administration has carefully examined the "extreme tail risk" scenario where the US takes military action against his country, and had prepared accordingly, without providing further detail.

"I think you have a responsibility in these roles to look at extreme tail risk," Carney told the Times. "That's just risk management. That's not a base case, but it would be irresponsible not to" prepare.

Tensions between the neighbouring countries have flared under US President Donald Trump.

Why Canada is seeing its biggest military recruitment surge in 30 years

On patrol with Canadian forces securing the Arctic as global threats grow

Canada orders 12 submarines from Germany in largest defence deal of its kind

Any conflict would likely be highly imbalanced. The US military has more than 2 million active-duty and reserve troops, while Canada has fewer than 200,000, according to their governments. Similarly, as of 2024, the US possessed 65 military submarines, compared to Canada's four.

Canada, though, has the longest coastline in the world and is close to the Arctic, two circumstances that have prompted Carney to boost defence spending since he took office.

Meanwhile, Trump has frequently talked about Canada as the "51st state". He also started a trade war with it that deepened last month as the two countries began exchanging tit-for-tat tariffs on a number of products.

Even since then, Carney told the Times, he speaks with Trump "frequently".

"From my perspective, we have a good relationship in the sense of we can pick up the phone and talk to each other about issues," he told the outlet.

"He's direct. I'm direct in terms of where positions are. It's much more efficient that way, and so you know that exists and that will continue to exist."

Carney said he believed there was still a path to resume trade negotiations with the US. Returning to their amicable ties would be beneficial for both countries, he said.

articles.title: Mexico’s USMCA violations threaten American energy
articles.summary: U.S. and Mexican trade officials are set to meet in Washington this month to address Mexico’s alleged violation of USMCA commitments regarding discriminatory energy policies.
articles.body:
When U.S. and Mexican trade officials meet in Washington this month to continue the joint review of the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA), one unresolved trade issue should be at the top of the agenda: Mexico’s discriminatory treatment of American energy companies.

In his first term, President Trump secured historic commitments from Mexico in USMCA to open its energy markets to American investment and guarantee fair treatment for U.S. producers, but a deal is only as good as our willingness to enforce it. Although USMCA includes a clear dispute settlement chapter to resolve infractions, Mexico’s government has repeatedly violated the agreement since 2021 by enacting policies that gave its state-owned industries an unfair advantage over U.S. companies and undermined existing investments.

In 2021, the Mexican government enacted reforms that forced the country’s grid to prioritize electricity generated by its state-owned electric utility over private power generation. The Office of the U.S. Trade Representative challenged those policies in 2022 by opening consultations with Mexico — the first step in USMCA’s dispute process — but the administration stopped there. It never took the next step of requesting a formal dispute panel that could lead to meaningful enforcement.

In the meantime, Mexico went even further.

Changes to Mexico’s constitution in 2024 and new energy laws enacted in early 2025 expanded government control of the energy sector . Under the new framework, the state must account for at least 54 percent of the average electricity injected into the national grid each year, while greater regulatory authority has been consolidated under executive control.

By rigging the system in favor of its state-owned companies, Mexico is violating the fair-treatment commitments it made under USMCA and putting American energy companies at a competitive disadvantage. Oil and natural gas companies face new barriers involving exploration, drilling, refining, transportation, and market access. Wind and solar companies now face restrictions that limit their ability to generate and dispatch power. The result is less access for American energy companies, new barriers for U.S. energy exports, and fewer opportunities for our nation’s companies to invest, compete and grow.

Whatever the energy source, American companies cannot compete on a level playing field when a foreign government owns their competitor and writes the rules in its favor.

We come at energy policy from different perspectives and do not agree on every issue. But it’s our shared consensus that American companies should be able to invest and compete under clear, predictable rules — and that Mexico must live up to the commitments it made under USMCA.

The ongoing joint review gives the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative the opportunity to finally resolve this dispute, whether by ending Mexico’s discriminatory energy policies through negotiations or moving to formal dispute settlement. Congress should provide the administration every resource it needs to achieve this mission.

The bipartisan Mexican Energy Trade Enforcement Act would give the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative additional support to reverse Mexico’s energy investment barriers now entrenched in their law. The legislation gives the Trump administration the full backing of Congress to hold Mexico accountable and eliminate its USMCA violations in the energy sector.

Mexico is one of America’s most important economic partners, and we want more North American energy trade and investment, not less. Partnership cannot mean enjoying the benefits of USMCA while ignoring the commitments that come with them.

The future of North American energy trade — and the credibility of USMCA itself — depend on whether we are willing to enforce the deal we made.

Jodey Arrington is serving the 19th District of Texas in Congress. He is the chairman of the House Budget Committee and a senior member of the House Ways & Means Committee. Amy Andryszak is president and CEO of the Interstate Natural Gas Association of America, the leading trade association representing America’s natural gas pipeline industry. Jason Grumet is CEO of the American Clean Power Association, the leading trade association representing the U.S. clean energy industry.

articles.title: Iranian-American group sues Trump over war
articles.summary: Plaintiffs have families in Iran who have been harmed by the US war, they say.
articles.body:
A group of Iranian Americans have filed a lawsuit against United States President Donald Trump, asking a court to order a halt to military action against Iran that they allege is harming them and their families and is in violation of constitutional war powers checks.

The complaint, filed in a Washington, DC, court on Thursday by the advocacy group National Iranian American Council (NIAC), argues the war will continue indefinitely and “cause imminent threats to the lives, limbs, health, property, and bare necessities” of Iranians, as well as Iranian Americans whom the organisation represents.

The lawsuit details the impact the war, which has raged on for more than six months now, has had on several of its members, including US citizens and a US Army veteran, and their families who are still inside Iran.

The relatives of some plaintiffs were allegedly killed or injured in air strikes during the war, including while in their homes, or as they went about doing routine tasks.

The plaintiffs also allege greater effects on themselves and their families, such as economic difficulties caused by US sanctions, and the inability to access adequate healthcare, or travel amid an expanding sanctions regime.

Those still inside Iran, the lawsuit says, are in danger because the Trump administration is continuing the war without legal oversight or proper authorisation. Thousands of civilians, including hundreds of children, have been killed by the US in the war so far, according to the lawsuit, and others are at risk.

“They are all in imminent danger of harm to their persons and properties proximately caused by the unconstitutional war waged by defendant President Donald J. Trump,” the complaint says.

In September, a United Nations fact-finding mission said the US likely committed “war crimes” in Iran, including in air strikes that allegedly killed hundreds of civilians.

“No President should have the power to take this country into an indefinite war by himself,” NIAC President Jamal Abdi said in a statement on Thursday. “This lawsuit asks a fundamental question: can one person decide, on his own, to keep an entire nation at war?”

On Tuesday, Trump told world leaders at the United Nations General Assembly that he was considering whether to “annihilate” Iran if Tehran did not return to talks and reach a deal with the US to end the war.

articles.title: Ethiopian army says 272 Tigrayan fighters killed in Amhara
articles.summary: Tigray People’s Liberation Front says in a ‘situation of full-blown war’ with Ethiopia’s government.
articles.body:
Ethiopia’s army says it has killed at least 272 fighters from the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF) in a counter-offensive in the country’s northwest Amhara region.

The Ethiopian National Defence Force said on Thursday that another 260 Tigrayan fighters were wounded and several were captured.

“Government forces launched a counter-offensive that inflicted heavy personnel and equipment losses on the TPLF” after the group and its allies attacked several areas of North Wollo, a region of Amhara that borders Tigray, the army said in a statement on Facebook.

The intensification came days after TPLF and six other armed groups from across Ethiopia announced the formation of the Ethiopian Peoples’ Forces Alliance for Survival, which committed itself to removing Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed’s government.

The coalition brought together the newly-formed Amhara Fano National Movement, the Oromo Liberation Army and other movements from the Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz regional states.

“We are in the situation of full-blown war now,” TPLF Vice President Amanuel Assefa told AFP news agency on Thursday.

He confirmed that Tigrayan forces were fighting alongside local armed groups in Afar and Amhara.

The alliance marks a striking realignment that had been almost a year in the making, bringing together armed groups with very different histories and grievances against the central government, including forces with histories of conflict among themselves.

In a statement issued as the fighting widened on Wednesday , the alliance said the federal government was attacking its forces on several fronts and presented their response as part of the broader struggle that had brought the coalition together.

Meanwhile, the escalation has disrupted air travel, as Tigrayan forces seized three local airports in the region.

Flights to Lalibela, a UNESCO-listed site in Amhara known for its medieval rock-hewn churches, were suspended on Thursday, according to Reuters news agency.

AFP also received reports of fighting around Lalibela, causing its airport to close. The area has often been targeted by the Fano, a local armed group that is now operating alongside the TPLF.

TPLF last went ⁠to war with the Ethiopian federal government in 2020, leading to a devastating two-year conflict that ended with a peace deal in 2022.

In his address at the UN General Assembly on Wednesday, Ethiopia’s President Taye Atske-Selassie Amde blamed the escalation on “the forces of destruction and mayhem” and “interference in our internal affairs by adversarial elements”.

He said Ethiopia had exercised “immense restraint” and made progress with its neighbours.

Analysts say the Tigray rebels have support from Eritrea, which fears landlocked Ethiopia is planning to invade its territory to gain access to the Red Sea.

The TPLF’s Assefa told AFP “we have no information about Eritrea’s plan”. Asked if they would request Eritrean intervention, he said: “Not yet.”

Ethiopia’s domestic conflicts are becoming harder to separate from wider rivalries in the Horn of Africa, particularly Addis Ababa’s deteriorating relationship with Eritrea and Sudan’s civil war.

Sudan’s army chief Abdel Fattah al-Burhan has visited Asmara twice since July for talks with Eritrean President Isaias Afwerki, while Sudan’s paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF) commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as Hemedti, reportedly visited Addis Ababa in late August.

articles.title: Macklemore announces Free Palestine tour
articles.summary: Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran’s tour after making pro-Palestine statements at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey.
articles.body:
( NewsNation ) — Rapper Macklemore announced Thursday that he will hold a Free Palestine tour.

“What happened to me is bigger than one artist or one stage,” he wrote on social platform X . “When the billionaire class can decide which voices are allowed on stage and which are too dangerous to hear, everyone should be paying attention.”

“So, we’re going on tour,” the rapper, born Benjamin Haggerty, continued. “All proceeds will benefit organizations supporting the Palestinian people and movement.”

Earlier this month, Macklemore was removed from Ed Sheeran’s Loop tour after making pro-Palestine statements at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. The move led some groups to speak out against the musician, calling for his removal from the tour. Among those who called for his removal was the owner of the New England Patriots and Gillette Stadium, Robert Kraft.

“Free Palestine, I said free Palestine,” he said at the opening of his song “Hind’s Hall.”

“I want those words to be loud and clear so that the people in Gaza all the way to the occupied West Bank, know that we have not forgotten them,” the “Thrift Shop” singer added.

He later posted a video of the remarks on online , writing, “Wanting all humans to be treated equal should never be controversial.”

In the days following his removal from the tour, all of Sheeran’s supporting acts withdrew from the tour. Sheeran issued a statement on Instagram where he explained that multiple venues threatened to pull out of the tour if Macklemore was not removed .

“Macklemore coming off tour was the promoter’s decision; it was not mine,” Sheeran wrote in a lengthy post, detailing how he tried to mend the situation without Macklemore’s removal. “Macklemore’s contract with the tour was with the promoter, not with me.”

In the post, Sheeran expressed a desire to not use his public platform to promote political purposes , saying his audience includes young people who do not come to the shows expecting a political forum.

The “Photograph” and “Shape of You” singer later addressed fans at a concert in Philadelphia on Saturday, apologizing for mistakes and breaking his silence on the Israel-Palestine conflict.

“What happened in Israel at the Nova Music Festival on Oct. 7, 2023, was horrific and compounded centuries of Jewish pain,” Sheeran said. “What is happening in Gaza is catastrophic and unjustifiable and disproportionate; my heart has been broken by the scale of the devastation and loss of civilian life and children’s lives.”

“The systematic injustice we see unfolding in the West Bank cannot be overlooked,” he continued. “I am already speaking with people across the spectrum to work out how to make a contribution that helps victims of these terrible times and listening and learning because I do not know enough.”

The Macklemore and Friends Free Palestine Tour will begin in Dublin on Oct. 26 before performing in Paris on Oct. 29 and London on Oct. 30. No other tour dates or locations have been listed at this time.

articles.title: First results declared Isle of Man general election
articles.summary: Results are in for Douglas South and Onchan with 10 constituencies still to declare.
articles.body:
Onchan has been the first constituency to declare elected candidates in the 2026 general election, followed closely by Douglas South.

Onchan has elected scientist Rachel Glover and Rob Callister keeps his seat, meaning that former education minister Julie Edge has not been re-elected.

Meanwhile, both Sarah Maltby and Claire Christian keep their seats in the first of the four constituencies in the capital to vote.

There are 82 candidates contesting the election for the 24 seats available in the House of Keys.

Exit polls conducted by Manx Radio predict seven outgoing MHKs will lose their seats, three of whom are current members of the Council of Ministers.

They suggest outgoing Environment, Food and Agriculture Minister Clare Barber, Education, Sport and Culture Minister Daphne Caine, and Enterprise Minister Tim Johnston have lost their seats.

Former ministers Onchan MHK Julie Edge, Ramsey MHK Lawrie Hooper and Rushen MHK Michelle Haywood, and deputy speaker of the Keys are also predicted to lose their seats.

In Ayre and Michael, the exit polls predict that Chief Minister Alfred Cannan is in a fight to retain his place in the House of Keys, with only 1% between him and the candidate in third.

Overall the exit polls suggest there will be 15 new MHKs, including eight women, down from 10 elected in 2021.

A third of the seats in the Keys are not being contested by outgoing MHKs, which means there is guaranteed to be eight new faces in Tynwald.

Arbory, Castletown and Malew: Kirrie Jenkins and too close to call between Jason Moorhouse and Steve Crowther.

Ayre and Michael: Stephen Broad and too close to call between Alfred Cannon and Phil Corkhill

Douglas Central: Peter Shimmin and Chris Thomas

Douglas East: Andy Saunders and too close to call between Joney Faragher and Dave Mackey

Douglas North: David Ashford and Damien Ciappelli

Douglas South: Sarah Maltby and Claire Christian

Garff: Richard Henthorne and Aishlinn Creer

Glenfaba and Peel: Katryna Baptist and Geoffrey Pugh

Middle: Jane Poole-Wilson and James Cochrane

Ramsey: Juan McGuinness and Robert Cowell

Rushen: Michael Crowe and too close to call between Mark Kemp and Simon Williams

Among the issues dominating the election in 2026 were keeping young people on the island, the availability and cost of housing, wind farms, healthcare waiting times, and the impacts of spiralling expenses for small businesses.

Voting took place across the island from 08:00 BST on Thursday until the polls closed at 20:00.

Those who have been elected as a Member of the House of Keys (MHK) will be sworn in on Tuesday by the first and second deemsters.

The House of Keys will then sit on 13 October to nominate a chief minister and speaker of the House of Keys.

articles.title: An Iowa rescue mission is closing its downtown thrift store and turning the retail floor into a 46-bed emergency shelter; the move will also free space for 25 beds for women and children
articles.summary: As winter approaches, a rescue mission in Dubuque, Iowa, is making a major change to its downtown operations to create more emergency shelter space.
articles.body: As winter approaches, a rescue mission in Dubuque, Iowa, is making a major change to its downtown operations to create more emergency shelter space. The Dubuque Rescue Mission plans to close its downtown thrift store and convert the retail floor into a 46-bed emergency shelter for men. The move is also expected to free up another space that can be used by Opening Doors, a local organisation serving women and children experiencing homelessness. According to a report by KCRG, the changes are being driven by rising demand for shelter and concerns about people being left without a safe place to stay during freezing weather.Thrift store space will become emergency shelterThe Dubuque Rescue Mission is preparing to close Thrift Store 1 at 398 Main St. The final day of sales is scheduled for October 3, after which the retail floor will be transformed into emergency accommodation capable of housing up to 46 men each night. The mission has already stopped accepting thrift-store donations at the Main Street location.The decision comes as the organisation faces increased demand for its services. KCRG reported that monthly meal demand at the mission has doubled over the past year, increasing from about 2,500 meals to more than 5,000. Recent Point-in-Time counts cited by the station also indicate an increase in unsheltered homelessness in Dubuque County. The mission's own website confirms that the store is being closed specifically to create additional bed space because of the continued need for shelter in Dubuque. It says the space will instead be used to provide shelter during the winter.Winter demand is putting pressure on sheltersThe timing of the conversion is significant because demand for emergency shelter typically rises as temperatures fall. The City of Dubuque's 2026-2030 Consolidated Plan notes that men's emergency shelter beds can reach capacity during the winter months and that the Rescue Mission has previously expanded its capacity to provide overflow accommodation during periods of high need.Rev. Samuel Felderman, executive director of the Dubuque Rescue Mission, told KCRG that converting a retail floor into a residential shelter is more complicated than simply installing beds. The organisation must meet fire, safety and zoning requirements while ensuring that the new shelter is secure and suitable for people staying there. The mission expects the project to require changes to the ground-floor space before it can be used as residential accommodation.The change will create space for women and childrenThe impact of the project will extend beyond the new men's shelter. Once men can be accommodated in the former thrift-store space, the mission's existing warming-centre space at Jackson and 16th streets can be made available to Opening Doors.Opening Doors is a Dubuque nonprofit that provides housing and support services to women and children experiencing homelessness and poverty. The organisation operates emergency, transitional and permanent supportive housing programmes in the community. According to KCRG, Opening Doors will use the freed-up space to add 25 beds for women and children. Together, the changes involving the two organisations are expected to expand local emergency housing capacity by up to 50 beds. The expansion comes as local shelters continue to deal with limited capacity. Both the organisations had to turn away people seeking refuge during extreme cold last winter because available space was limited.What happens to thrift-store donations?Although Thrift Store 1 is closing, the mission's broader donation and thrift operations will continue. The Dubuque Rescue Mission operates another thrift store at 998 Central Ave., which will continue accepting certain categories of donated goods, including furniture, lamps, books and other larger household items.The organisation is also directing donations intended for women and children to partner locations. Its website lists several community organisations where such donations can still be made, while donations intended for residents of the Rescue Mission, including men's clothing, towels, toiletries and twin-size bedding, can still be brought to the Main Street building.Mission seeks funding for the winter transitionAccording to the Dubuque Rescue Mission’s website, the organisation is seeking $250,000 from the community by October 31 to help cover construction, beds and operating costs associated with the new shelter. The funding effort comes as the organisation prepares the space for winter use. The project represents a broader effort among Dubuque organisations to respond to growing demand for emergency housing. Rather than adding a completely new building, the Rescue Mission is repurposing an existing downtown commercial space, while the resulting shift allows another organisation to increase shelter capacity for women and children.With the October 3 thrift-store closure approaching, the focus is now on completing the required work and preparing the 46-bed facility before winter conditions increase the need for emergency shelter across Dubuque.You use AI every day. articles.title: Iranian president says country wants deal with US made before midterms
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Thursday that Tehran is willing to strike a deal with the U.S. before the November midterms, pushing back on President Trump’s claim that the regime is waiting until after Americans hit the polls to settle the conflict. “We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian told reporters…
articles.body:
Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian said Thursday that Tehran is willing to strike a deal with the U.S. before the November midterms, pushing back on President Trump’s claim that the regime is waiting until after Americans hit the polls to settle the conflict.

“We don’t want it to get to the midterm elections,” Pezeshkian told reporters on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly.

He called for the U.S. to return to a memorandum of understanding reached in June that set the framework for a temporary ceasefire, before it ultimately fell apart.

Pezeshkian’s remarks directly counter Trump’s prediction that a deal between the U.S. and Iran could be reached after the fall elections.

“They’re waiting to see how I do in the midterm election,” Trump said in a speech to world leaders at the U.N.

The White House responded to Pezeshkian’s comments by criticizing Iran’s conduct during the war.

“The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region,” White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said in a statement to NBC News.

“The President is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable,” she added.

Trump envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner held lengthy indirect talks with Iranian officials Tuesday during the U.N. gathering.

Witkoff later said he hoped the discussions would prove “constructive and promising” in securing a path to end the more than six-month conflict.

Trump, meanwhile, has continued to threaten further military action if Iran refuses to reach an agreement over its nuclear program. He told world leaders that Tehran could make a deal or face “annihilation.”

Pezeshkian rejected that pressure in his own U.N. address Wednesday, saying Iran would not surrender or abandon its nuclear program.

“We will never bow our head or bend at the knee,” he said.

But Pezeshkian also suggested Iran remained willing to negotiate, provided it was not forced to do so under threat.

articles.title: Netanyahu slams critics, Mamdani in defiant speech as UN delegates walk out
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a defiant speech at the United Nations General Assembly, defending Israel’s actions against Iran and its proxy forces across the Middle East, as several delegates staged a walkout. Netanyahu appeared in New York while the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him loomed. The body accused…
articles.body:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu delivered a defiant speech at the United Nations General Assembly, defending Israel’s actions against Iran and its proxy forces across the Middle East, as several delegates staged a walkout.

Netanyahu appeared in New York while the subject of an International Criminal Court arrest warrant against him loomed. The body accused the prime minister of facilitating war crimes throughout Israel’s military operation in the Gaza Strip, triggered by Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attack against the country.

“On that darkest of days, our enemies expected us to collapse,” Netanyahu said in his speech.

“Well, we didn’t collapse. Instead, we rose and fought like lions for the past three years. Our heroic soldiers have fought day in and day out in a seven-front war.”

Netanyahu began his remarks urging “moral cowards” to exit the General Assembly Hall alongside the diplomats who had already boycotted his speech. The Israeli delegation whooped and cheered for Netanyahu, chanting in Hebrew, “The people of Israel live.”

The Israeli leader, who is under intense isolation globally — including unfavorable views from the majority of Americans — took aim at one of his most high-profile U.S. critics, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D).

Mamdani had called for the U.S. to act on the ICC arrest warrant when the Israeli leader arrived in the country for the U.N. meeting.

“To all those spreading these lies about my country and about our brave soldiers, whether they sit in this hall or in the office of the antisemitic mayor of New York, I say this: Shame on you!” Netanyahu said.

“Mr. Mamdani, you try to stop me from coming here. You try to silence me. Well, you can’t silence me,” Netanyahu continued, also rejecting the mayor and other critics’ allegations that Israel committed genocide against Palestinians in Gaza.

Netanyahu argued Israel has no choice but to defend itself against Palestinian attacks in the West Bank, “militias” in Syria, the Houthis in Yemen and Iranian forces, as well as to counter Hezbollah in Lebanon.

While American delegates at the U.N. stayed and applauded Netanyahu’s speech, the Israeli leader appears increasingly isolated from President Trump and his administration. While Netanyahu traveled to the White House after his 2025 speech at the U.N., he will not do so this year — carrying out a shortened agenda in the U.S. as Trump left to welcome Chinese President Xi Jinping in Washington.

Israeli and American officials said there was no time for Trump and Netanyahu to meet, pointing to the High Holy Days in the Jewish calendar and the Israeli prime minister’s ongoing reelection bid. Israel’s elections are set for October.

articles.title: We aren’t trying to kill Trump, Iran’s president insists to reporters at New York hotel
articles.summary: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian sat down to face questions from a group of journalists in New York on Thursday amid the war with the US.
articles.body: Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian’s media appearances in Iran are tightly controlled affairs. But on Thursday he sat down to face questions from a group of journalists in New York, where despite being the leader of a country at war with the United States, he is visiting with the protection of the US Secret Service. In the wide-ranging session, a day after addressing the UN General Assembly, Pezeshkian repeated familiar Iranian positions on the war, its nuclear program and dissent in Iran. He also talked about the effect of sanctions on the Iranian people, and claimed Iran would never try to kill Donald Trump – despite the president and US authorities accusing the regime of plotting his assassination. The comments were made at the Millennium Hilton hotel, a stone’s throw from the UN headquarters where the Iranian president declared Wednesday that his country “will not bow down” as the war with the US drags on. In the briefing, Pezeshkian also described recent meetings he had held with Iran’s Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, who has not been seen in public since the outset of the war, saying that the leader was “quite healthy.” There has been mounting speculation in recent months over Khamenei’s health, after he was understood to have sustained serious injuries in the US-Israeli attack that killed his father and predecessor Ali Khamenei at the beginning of the conflict in February. Speaking about Khamenei’s condition, Pezeshkian said, “I did not see any major challenges with his health or physical appearance,” adding that their most recent in-person meeting had taken place around one month ago and lasted around seven hours. Pezeshkian said the pair had sat on pillows on the ground and stood up to walk around during the meeting. US intelligence assesses that despite his injuries Khamenei is still playing a critical role in shaping war strategy alongside senior Iranian officials, multiple sources familiar with the intelligence said in May. A meeting in Manhattan The presence of Iran’s delegation in a country with which it remains at war is already virtually unprecedented. But this spectacle became increasingly unconventional on Thursday when the Iranian president and Iran’s Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi briefed reporters including from CNN in a hotel function room in Midtown Manhattan. A State Department official said earlier this week that the visiting Iranian delegates were “being admitted to the United States strictly for the purpose of representing the Islamic Republic of Iran before the United Nations” and that they must “restrict their activities to United Nations-related business only.” The Iranians “must seek and receive approval in advance” from the State Department if they want to travel outside the vicinity of the UN headquarters, John F. Kennedy International Airport or Iran’s UN mission facilities, the official said. In the briefing, Pezeshkian denied accusations that Iran was trying to kill the president, saying it has “never been the position [of the Iranian government], overtly or covertly, to seek to assassinate Trump or his family members.” Last month, the US Secret Service said it was aware of a video aired by Iran’s state broadcaster appearing to threaten the life of Barron Trump, the president’s youngest son. This came after Israel shared intelligence with the US that Iran had devised a plan to assassinate Donald Trump. In late 2024, the US Justice Department announced federal charges over what it described as a thwarted Iranian plot to kill Trump before the presidential election. Hard-line Iranian media have repeatedly featured content threatening the life of Trump and his family. During funeral events for the late Khamenei in July, regime loyalists were seen holding posters with the words “Kill Trump.” Trump has publicly discussed the Iranian threats on his life too, saying in July: “I’m on whatever list … so far, I guess I’ve been a bit lucky, but maybe that doesn’t last very long. These are evil, sick people.” In response to Pezeshkian’s comments, White House spokesperson Anna Kelly said, “The Iranian regime has murdered thousands of its own people, killed Americans overseas, executed acts of terrorism in the Strait of Hormuz, and launched indiscriminate attacks against its neighbors in the region.” “The president is courageously ensuring that such an evil country never possesses a nuclear weapon, which will make the entire world safer and more stable,” Kelly said. ‘We have problems’ Pezeshkian also discussed the domestic challenges facing Iran. US sanctions and the ongoing war have suffocated the country’s economy, sparking prices increases and shortages of basic necessities. The Iranian president also said in the session that Iran wants a deal, but that any agreement was not related to the timing of the US midterms. Iran’s economy was in a dire state even before the war began, with the poor conditions a key driving factor behind the anti-regime demonstrations which kicked off in the Iranian capital city Tehran in 2025. “We have problems. Unprecedentedly difficult problems,” he told reporters, while referring to US sanctions as a “silent murderous campaign.” Much like in his Wednesday address to world leaders, Pezeshkian appeared confident in the briefing that Iran would prevail despite the challenges facing his country. He also insisted that US bases in the region were legitimate targets as they had been used to attack Iran. “Most of the American bases in the region are no longer useable,” he claimed. Iranian strikes damaged and destroyed hundreds of buildings and structures at US bases across the Middle East region during the war’s first months, according to an official Pentagon watchdog report released earlier this month. “Of course, the US has the power to destroy anything anywhere, but it is impossible to bring about Iranian surrender,” Pezeshkian said.

articles.title: He quit school at 12 to bag peanuts; 22 years later, he runs a Texas farm with organic crops and a 16-acre vineyard
articles.summary: Henry Froese was told he couldn't farm without family ties, couldn't grow organic crops in Gaines County's sandy soils, and certainly couldn't grow grapes
articles.body: Henry Froese was told he couldn't farm without family ties, couldn't grow organic crops in Gaines County's sandy soils, and certainly couldn't grow grapes there. His answer was always "Why not?" According to Farm Progress, Froese quit school at 12 to bag peanuts for a local farmer, later leased his own land, and over the past 22 years built an operation that now spans organic and conventional peanuts, cotton, livestock and a 16-acre vineyard, earning him the 2026 Peanut Efficiency Award for the Southwest.From bagging peanuts as a boy to running his own operationHenry's history in farming began at age 12, when he quit school to load "50-pound bags of peanuts" for a local farmer, simply because all he wanted to do was work. "Not much has changed," he told Farm Progress. "I'm still doing the same thing today," except now he loads his own planter on his own land. In 2004, farm boss Brett Woods leased him land and equipment, land Henry owns today. By 2012, he produced his first organic peanut crop, yielding nearly 5,000 pounds per acre, setting the course for everything that followed.Building Y Knot Farms and a 16-acre vineyard from marginal groundToday, Henry and his wife, Marie, run "Y Knot Farms" and "Y Knot Vineyard" near Seagraves, Texas. In 2022, the couple planted a vineyard on 5 acres of marginal cropland; it has since grown to 16 acres across five grape varieties. Alongside organic Spanish and conventional Virginia peanuts, Henry grows cotton, sorghum, sunflowers, wheat and rye, and the family raises Red Angus cattle, Dorper sheep, horses and Kunekune pigs. Marie leads the vineyard and handles the operation's extensive organic paperwork, while also raising their four children and running the family's event venue.Farming with sustainability, water conservation and soil health in mindHenry makes every production decision with the future in mind, calling long-term sustainability the focus of everything he does. Much of his land relies on centre-pivot and drip irrigation drawn from the region's depleting Ogallala Aquifer, a resource he's outspoken about protecting. He's meticulous about repairing sprinkler leaks and weighs every choice against water availability. articles.title: Angel mom says blue-state DAs are putting illegal immigrant criminals before public safety
articles.summary: Cheryl Minter's Change.org petition targets Fairfax County prosecutor Steve Descano after her daughter's accused killer had over 30 prior arrests.
articles.body: A Virginia mother whose daughter was stabbed to death at a bus stop is fighting to oust the county's top prosecutor after learning the accused killer had been arrested more than 30 times before the attack. "Stephanie should be alive today," Cheryl Minter wrote in a petition calling for Fairfax County Commonwealth's Attorney Steve Descano to be removed. "I had to do what no parent should ever have to. I had to bury my daughter." Stephanie Minter, 41, was found with multiple stab wounds inside a bus stop shelter in Hybla Valley on Feb. 23, Fairfax County police said. Abdul Jalloh, 32, is charged with second-degree murder. He has not been convicted in her death. "She was an amazingly strong woman, amazingly strong, and happy, and brought brightness and joy to so many people," Cheryl Minter told Fox News Digital. SOROS-BACKED DA'S LAX ILLEGAL IMMIGRATION POLICIES LED TO 'PREVENTABLE' BUS STOP STABBING MURDER: COMPLAINT The Department of Homeland Security says Jalloh, a Sierra Leone national who entered the U.S. illegally in 2012, had been arrested more than 30 times. His previous charges included rape, malicious wounding, assault and theft, DHS said. SANCTUARY COUNTY REFUSED 615 ICE TRANSFER REQUESTS, TURNED OVER JUST 11 ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS, RECORDS SHOW "I was shocked. I mean, literally in shock," Cheryl Minter said when asked about his record. "And then this man who's killed her, just is let off like it's nothing. Like it's nothing." In her petition, Cheryl Minter blamed Descano's decisions for what she called a preventable death. "Thirty times the system had a chance to stop him. Thirty times," she wrote. "I think about that every single day." JORDAN GRILLS SOROS-BACKED DA DESCANO IN HEATED SPAT OVER SOFT-ON-CRIME POLICY: 'THIS IS ALMOST LAUGHABLE' Cheryl questioned why Jalloh was released after an arrest she recalled from the winter before Stephanie's death. The details of that case and who made the release decision have not been independently confirmed. "When you let these people back out on the streets, they're not gonna stop. Why would they stop?" she said. Cheryl Minter also pointed to Descano's 2020 plea bargaining policy. It told prosecutors to "consider immigration consequences where possible" and weigh how the charges could affect a defendant's immigration status, WTOP reported. The outlet reported in May that the webpage detailing the policy was no longer publicly available on Descano's office website. Cheryl Minter argues that prosecutors should put public safety first. That policy is under federal scrutiny. The Justice Department announced in May that it was investigating whether Descano's office gave defendants who are in the country illegally preferential treatment over U.S. citizens in charging decisions and plea deals. The department said it had reached no conclusions. The investigation does not establish how Jalloh's earlier cases were handled. SOROS-BACKED PROSECUTOR SET FOR CAPITOL HILL GRILLING AS SANCTUARY POLICIES FACE RECKONING Descano defended the policy after receiving notice of the investigation. "My policies are fair, legal, and reflect the values of my community," he wrote in a post on X. Asked what she wants from her petition, Cheryl Minter said her priority is changing those practices in Fairfax County and beyond. She also wants Descano out of office. SOROS-BACKED DA ACCUSED OF GOING EASY ON ILLEGAL IMMIGRANTS GETS SQUEEZED BY HOUSE GOP "I think first and foremost is the change," she said. "Second would be, I would love to see Descano out." Jennifer Harrison, executive director of the Victims' Rights Reform Council, helped Cheryl Minter start the Change.org petition. Cheryl Minter said she knows an online petition cannot itself remove Descano, but hopes it will drive scrutiny of his office. Congress is also pressing Descano for answers. House Judiciary Committee Chairman Jim Jordan, R-Ohio, subpoenaed him on Sept. 16 as part of an investigation into whether prosecutors give preferential treatment to criminal suspects because of their immigration status. Jordan set a Sept. 25 deadline after accusing Descano's office of failing to fully comply with earlier requests. In a previous statement to Fox News Digital, Descano's office called the subpoena a "needless escalation" and accused the committee of waging a "partisan siege" against Fairfax County. It said the office had turned over more than 1,100 pages of documents, that Descano had voluntarily testified, and that it would continue to respond to legitimate inquiries while working to keep the county safe. The office has separately said it is prosecuting Jalloh for Stephanie's murder, with a trial scheduled for January 2027, and cannot comment further on the pending case. WATCH: SOROS PROSECUTOR’S HEARING DEVOLVES INTO ANGRY CHAOS OVER ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT RAPE CASE: 'BE QUIET!' Fairfax County police said Jalloh was arrested after an employee at a local business recognized him and called authorities the day after Stephanie Minter was killed. He was held without bond. ICE lodged a detainer on Feb. 25, after Jalloh was in custody, asking to be notified before his release, according to DHS. The agency said it had also lodged a detainer against him in 2020 and that an immigration judge later ordered him removed to a country other than Sierra Leone. Cheryl Minter said employees of Descano's office working on her daughter's murder case have been "wonderful with me." She said her criticism is aimed at the decisions she believes left a repeat offender free. "I want people never to stop talking about it," she said. "I just don't want the talk to stop, and I'll do whatever to keep it going." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Stephanie cannot speak for herself anymore. So I am," she wrote in the petition. Fox News Digital reached out to Descano's office for comment on Cheryl Minter's allegations and petition. Fox News Digital's Elizabeth Elkind contributed to this report.

articles.body:
The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to allow it to resume deporting migrants to countries where they have no ties.

President Trump has increasingly relied on the practice, called third-country removals, in his aggressive immigration crackdown. His administration has signed agreements to send deportees to countries across the globe, many in Africa.

For months, the flights have proceeded after the Supreme Court sided with the president at an earlier stage in the case.

The administration is bringing the case back to the justices after the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 1 st Circuit has once again ordered the flights to stop without giving migrants a better opportunity to raise claims they’ll be tortured. It’s the latest ruling in the monthslong legal challenge backed by immigration groups.

Solicitor General D. John Sauer wants the justices to immediately lift the ruling until they can hear the administration’s appeal. He said the ruling is causing “chaos” and already forced DHS to cancel a flight to three countries carrying 70 people with criminal convictions.

“The unexpected springing-back of district court’s order has, this Office is informed,” Sauer wrote, “created substantial logistical problems with ongoing removal operations—including the cancellation of flights—and led to added expense, potential diplomatic issues, and the inability to remove dangerous criminals.”

The case heads to Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson, who by default handles emergency matters arising from the 1 st Circuit. She ordered the plaintiffs respond in writing by Monday afternoon. Jackson could act alone or refer the case to the full court for a vote.

Since retaking office, the Trump administration has sought the Supreme Court’s emergency intervention more than three dozen times after lower judges have blocked aspects of the president’s agenda. The justices are still mulling their ruling in a separate emergency case, which concerns DHS’s desire to overhaul a key immigration database in time for the midterms.

Last year, the administration brought the battle over third-country removals to the Supreme Court at an earlier stage in the legal challenge. The court at that time lifted a judge’s temporary block on the flights over the dissents of the liberal justices. Days later, the court again ruled in favor of Trump, rejecting the judge’s insistence that a deportation flight to South Sudan had defied him.

The Supreme Court’s orders have effectively enabled the deportations to continue since last summer.

The high court is now being asked to consider the final ruling from the judge, Brian Murphy, an appointee of former President Biden who serves in Boston. The 1 st Circuit upheld it last week. Late Wednesday, it clarified that meant the administration had to stop the flights and couldn’t pursue plans to deport a Peruvian man to the Central African Republic.

“The district court has now tripled down, entering final judgment in favor of respondents and awarding substantially the same relief on substantially the same grounds,” Sauer wrote.

Murphy’s ruling found DHS must provide migrants certain procedures so they can raise a claim that they will be tortured if deported to the third country. The Trump administration says it only will deport them to countries that have “credibly assured” Secretary of State Marco Rubio that it will not persecute them.
